guarantees.claim: For each i in 0..NumAlerts-1, an instance of prim_alert_sender is generated, driving alert_tx_o[i] according to its internal logic.
All generated alert sender instances have their alert_req_i input connected to the single signal alerts[0], not indexed by i.

assumptions.claim: alerts[0] is driven externally with a valid alert request that meets the protocol of prim_alert_sender.
assumptions.risk: If alerts has more than one bit and the indexed alert[i] is meant, the wrong request triggers all senders; conversely, if alerts is a single-bit broadcast it is correct but the design intent is unclear.

assumptions.claim: AlertAsyncOn[i] parameter correctly configures the synchronizer bypass for each alert sender based on clock-domain requirements.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect AsyncOn setting could cause metastability or timing violations in the alert path.

uncertain_points.claim: It is unclear whether connecting all alert_req_i inputs to alerts[0] is intentional or a mistake (possibly alerts[i] was intended).
uncertain_points.cond: when NumAlerts > 1 and alerts is a multi-bit bus
uncertain_points.risk: Could cause all alert senders to fire on a single request instead of individually, or leave higher-indexed alert requests unused, leading to missed alerts.

uncertain_points.claim: The prim_alert_sender outputs alert_ack_o and alert_state_o are left unconnected; no logic monitors the acknowledgment or internal state of the alert senders.
uncertain_points.risk: A stuck or failed alert sender may not be detected; alert transmission could silently fail, breaking the safety/security alert path.
